output.brief: The rejections came from a data error in our own paperwork, not from the fungicide, Lower Serra growers or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new Tallis system, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados and kept a 7.0°C carriage temperature. Our specification is 4.0°C. All five Meridane containers went out at 7°C and were rejected, with 9–14% decay. The four containers at 4°C were accepted, including three that used the new fungicide. Meridane's units held the temperature we gave them, so a claim against them would fail. Suspending Lower Serra growers would punish the wrong party. Lower Serra pallets were somewhat worse, but they were also in the accepted containers, so that is at most a secondary effect. Dropping the new fungicide would not fix anything. I'm quite sure of this (about 90%). Do now: correct the Tallis record to 4.0°C, and have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a pre-submission check of reefer settings against the product specification. Warn Nordhafen about the cause and the fix. Don't claim against Meridane, suspend growers, or penalise the contractor until the review of who signed off the data is done.
